lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 11: requests, limits and QoS classes
lesson.description: Give containers CPU and memory requests and limits, watch CPU throttling and an OOMKill on kind, read QoS classes, and meet LimitRange and ResourceQuota.
lesson.tested: Ran every example on kind v0.33.0, node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2, cgroup v2 node, 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Set requests so the scheduler can place you, set a memory limit you can live with, and remember that CPU over the limit slows down while memory over the limit gets killed.

boards.title: What the numbers mean
boards.hint: the scheduler counts requests; the kernel enforces limits

rows.name: requests
rows.role: What the scheduler reserves. Usage graphs will not explain a Pending Pod, because the scheduler counts requests.

rows.name: limits
rows.role: What the kernel enforces through cgroups.

rows.name: cpu: 500m
rows.role: Half a core. `1` is one core or vCPU.

rows.name: CPU at the limit
rows.role: The container is throttled and keeps running. Read `nr_throttled` and `throttled_usec`.

rows.name: Memory at the limit
rows.role: The container is OOM-killed. Exit code 137.

rows.name: Guaranteed
rows.role: Requests equal limits for cpu and memory, every container. Limits alone are copied to requests.

homework.intro: Use the kind cluster and the namespace `k8s-from-zero` from part 4. The lesson's node is `k8s-ep10-control-plane`, with 8 CPUs and about 16 GiB, and it is a cgroup v2 node. `kubectl top` is not available: kind does not install a metrics add-on. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What does the scheduler count, and what does the kernel enforce?
exercises.a: Requests are what the scheduler reserves. Limits are what the kernel enforces through cgroups.

exercises.q: At the limit, what happens to CPU, and what happens to memory?
exercises.a: CPU is throttled and the container keeps running. Memory gets the container OOM-killed with exit code 137.

exercises.q: Name the three QoS classes and the eviction order.
exercises.a: BestEffort, Burstable and Guaranteed. BestEffort goes first, Guaranteed last. The class comes from requests and limits and also sets OOM scores.

exercises.q: Where do you see a quota error on a Deployment?
exercises.a: On its ReplicaSet, not on the Deployment. Look for `exceeded quota`, or for an error about missing requests or limits if no LimitRange fills in defaults.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: A Pod stays Pending with `Insufficient cpu` or `Insufficient memory`. What does the lesson tell you to read, and why will a usage graph not explain it?
exercises.a: `Allocated resources` in `kubectl describe node`. The scheduler counts requests, not live usage. Lower the requests, free capacity, or add nodes.

exercises.q: RESTARTS climbs and lastState says OOMKilled with exit 137. What are the two responses in the lesson?
exercises.a: Raise the limit, and probably the request, or fix the leak. The app needed more memory than its limit, or it leaks.

exercises.q: `kubectl top` prints `error: Metrics API not available`. What does the lesson say to read instead?
exercises.a: The cgroup files, such as `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.stat`. `top` needs a metrics add-on that kind does not install. Part 25 installs metrics-server.
